title: Rigveda 5.67: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.67: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.67 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 386r-386v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.67.1-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 386v
translation.original_text:
1baḻ i̱tthā de̍va niṣkṛ̱tam ādi̍tyā yaja̱tam bṛ̱hat | varu̍ṇa̱ mitrārya̍ma̱n varṣi̍ṣṭhaṁ kṣa̱tram ā̍śāthe ||
2ā yad yoni̍ṁ hira̱ṇyaya̱ṁ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̱ sada̍thaḥ | dha̱rtārā̍ carṣaṇī̱nāṁ ya̱ntaṁ su̱mnaṁ ri̍śādasā ||
3viśve̱ hi vi̱śvave̍daso̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | vra̱tā pa̱deva̍ saścire̱ pānti̱ martya̍ṁ ri̱ṣaḥ ||
4te hi sa̱tyā ṛ̍ta̱spṛśa̍ ṛ̱tāvā̍no̱ jane̍-jane | su̱nī̱thāsa̍ḥ su̱dāna̍vo̱ 'ṁhoś ci̍d uru̱cakra̍yaḥ ||
5ko nu vā̍m mi̱trāstu̍to̱ varu̍ṇo vā ta̱nūnā̍m | tat su vā̱m eṣa̍te ma̱tir atri̍bhya̱ eṣa̍te ma̱tiḥ ||
translation.text:
1YE Gods, Âdityas, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Mitra, verily Have here obtained supremest sway, high, holy, set apart for you.
2When, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye sit in your golden dwelling-place, Ye Twain, supporters of mankind, foeslayers, give felicity.
3All these, possessors of all wealth, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Follow their ways, as if with feet, and guard from injury mortal man.
4For they are true, they cleave to Law, held holy among every race, Good leaders, bounteous in their gifts, deliverers even from distress.
5Which of your persons, Varuṇa or Mitra, merits not our praise? Therefore our thought is turned to you, the Atris' thought is turned to you.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 386v (numbered 59v by the scribe) (OPenn image 387, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.67.1 ‹-āśātheiti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 387r (numbered 60r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.68.2 ‹-itighṛta-yonī mitraḥ ca ubhā›. Verses 5.67.1-5 end on this page; 5.67.1 begins on fol. 386r (numbered 59r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
1baṭ | itthā | deva | niḥ-kṛtam | ādityā | yajatam | bṛhat | varuṇa | mitra | aryaman | varṣiṣṭham | kṣatram | āśātheiti
2ā | yat | yonim | hiraṇyayam | varuṇa | mitra | sadathaḥ | dhartārā | carṣaṇīnām | yantam | sumnam | riśādasā
3viśve | hi | viśva-vedasaḥ | varuṇaḥ | mitraḥ | aryamā | vratā | padāiva | saścire | pānti | martyam | riṣaḥ
4te | hi | satyāḥ | ṛta-spṛśaḥ | ṛta-vānaḥ | jane--jane | su-nīthāsaḥ | su-dānavaḥ | aṃhoḥ | cit | uru-cakrayaḥ
5kaḥ | nu | vām | mitra | astutaḥ | varuṇaḥ | vā | tanūnām | tat | su | vām | ā | īṣate | matiḥ | atri-bhyaḥ | ā | īṣate | matiḥ
